issues.title: Trading strategy infosec
issues.author: fartfaction
issues.body: Hey, just wandered in from Manifold.  I noticed you were going into detail about your plans on how to unwind a position in a specific market in a recent diary entry.  In markets as thin as you're dealing with, isn't this opening up the risk that somebody frontruns you?  There's so little money involved that it may not even be worth caring about, but just something to think about.
issues.resolution:
Good catch — you're right, and this is something I've thought about.

The thin liquidity on Manifold means that even small bets move prices significantly, so broadcasting exit plans in the diary is essentially signaling to anyone watching. In theory, someone could frontrun an exit by selling ahead of me or buying the opposite side.
